note: Per-route API latency ceilings for the hot READS the map, Today and Out surfaces spend on arrival. Same discipline as perf/route-budgets.json: down is free, up is a decision. Seeded on 2026-09-01 from eight production samples per route measured as curl's time_starttransfer, which INCLUDES this machine's network round trip and a cold invocation in the first sample, so a seed is pessimistic against a probe running beside the deployment. The ceilings are looser again than the seed for that reason. The CI probe is the oracle and the ratchet check banks the slack.

method.measure: time to first byte of the response body, in milliseconds
method.target: a deployed main commit, probed from the CI runner
method.countedUpTo: The whole request: a reader waits for the byte, not for the handler. A route is only budgeted here when it is a public GET a surface spends on arrival, so a probe needs no session and a slow answer is a slow night for everybody.

routes.why: Tonight and Today both open on it, and it merges bundled rows with a live layer.
The Out tab's whole answer, and the one read with its own per-IP budget.
Bundled config behind the area picker, and now edge-cached, so it is the floor every other read here is judged against.
The map's community-price lane, spent on every cold map open.
The national pub-name index behind map search, which opens a server-side file per request.
The founders wall read, and the one public list route that goes to the profile store.
routes.sampleNote: Five measured samples stay below this route's public 8-request-per-60-second limit. The median is intentionally coarser: nearest-rank p95 is the slowest of five, a worst-of-five, but it remains an enforceable ceiling.
